Question Choices: Fill: A sphere has a radius of 6. What is its volume? (Enter the coefficient of $\pi$ only)
Solution: Use (4/3)πr³. The coefficient of π is (4/3)×(6)³=288. The volume is (288)π cubic units. Enter only the coefficient: 288.

Question Choices: Fill: A cylinder has a volume of 150. What is the volume of a cone with the exact same radius and height?
Hints: A cone holds exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder
Solution: A cone with the same radius and perpendicular height has one third of the cylinder’s volume. Vcone=150÷3=50 cubic units.

Question Choices: Fill: A sphere has radius $r=3$. Volume is $\_\_\pi$. (Enter the number only)
Solution: Use (4/3)πr³. The coefficient of π is (4/3)×(3)³=36. The volume is (36)π cubic units. Enter only the coefficient: 36.

Question Choices: Fill: Find the volume of a cylinder if the Area of its circular base is 15 and its height is 6.
Hints: Just multiply the base area by the height
Solution: The circular base AREA is already 15; πr² has already been accounted for. Volume=B×h=15×6=90 cubic units. Do not multiply by π again.

Question Choices: Select the cylinder with the larger volume. A: radius 3, height 4. B: radius 4, height 3. ~~A | B~~
Hints: Calculate r²h for both cylinders; compare the coefficients because π is positive.
Solution: Cylinder volumes are πr²h. A=36π and B=48π. Since π is positive and 48>36, B has the larger volume. Compare both r²h products; radius alone does not determine volume.
